posts.title: Deploying High-Performance RAG Pipelines Across 1.5M+ Records with OpenAI and Pinecone
posts.summary: Architectural insights on building sub-100ms semantic search systems over massive product catalogs, hybrid search reranking, and vector caching strategies.
posts.author: Himanshu Ranjan
posts.content:
### The Challenge of Large-Scale Vector Retrieval

When scaling Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG) platforms beyond millions of documents—such as indexing 1.5M+ electronic product datasheets—naive cosine similarity over vector databases introduces latency bottlenecks and precision loss.

Here is how we architected a resilient, production-grade RAG pipeline capable of handling dense technical specs with high retrieval accuracy:

#### 1. Chunking with Context Preservation

Electronic components have intricate specifications (voltage ratings, pinouts, tolerance). Splitting text purely by character count destroys table semantics. We implemented AST-guided Markdown splitting:

```python
def chunk_datasheet_with_metadata(doc_text: str, component_id: str):
    # Extract top-level attributes
    header_context = extract_component_attributes(doc_text)
    chunks = semantic_text_splitter.split_text(doc_text)
    
    enriched_chunks = []
    for chunk in chunks:
        # Prepend contextual metadata to each vector chunk
        enriched = f"Component: {component_id} | Context: {header_context}\n{chunk}"
        enriched_chunks.append(enriched)
    return enriched_chunks
```

#### 2. Hybrid Search & Cross-Encoder Reranking

Pure dense embeddings struggle with exact alphanumeric part numbers (e.g. `STM32F401RE`). By combining **Sparse BM25** with **Dense Pinecone Vector Search** and feeding the top-50 results through a cross-encoder reranker, Top-3 retrieval precision surged from 71% to 94.6%.

#### 3. Semantic Vector Caching with Redis

Over 35% of customer queries share semantic equivalence. Storing normalized vector embeddings in Redis allows instantaneous cache hits without touching external LLM APIs.

posts.title: Mastering the Production MLOps Lifecycle: Continuous Training, DVC, and Evidently Drift Detection
posts.summary: How we orchestrate automated machine learning retraining workflows, detect data and concept drift, and maintain version control across datasets and models.
posts.author: Himanshu Ranjan
posts.content:
### Why Machine Learning Models Fail Silently in Production

Unlike traditional backend microservices that crash with clean stack traces, machine learning models degrade silently. When production data distributions drift away from training distributions, prediction accuracy plummets without throwing a single HTTP 500 error.

To solve this at scale, we constructed an end-to-end MLOps ecosystem utilizing **MLflow**, **DVC**, and **Evidently AI**.

#### 1. Data Version Control (DVC)

Every dataset iteration is versioned and tied directly to Git commit hashes. This guarantees complete auditability—every model artifact in our AWS S3 bucket can be traced back to the exact training data slice.

#### 2. Automated Drift Detection with Evidently AI

We schedule automated statistical tests (Kolmogorov-Smirnov and Population Stability Index) comparing sliding 24-hour inference logs against baseline training metrics. When drift exceeds a 0.05 p-value threshold, automated webhooks trigger retraining pipelines in AWS EventBridge.

posts.title: Deceiving Attackers at Scale: Engineering Adaptive SSH Honeypots with Cowrie and LLM Decoys
posts.summary: Building intelligent deception environments that capture zero-day attacker techniques using LLM-driven shell emulation and MITRE ATT&CK log correlation.
posts.author: Himanshu Ranjan
posts.content:
### Beyond Static Decoys

Traditional SSH honeypots rely on static file trees and hardcoded bash responses. Sophisticated adversaries immediately recognize the decoy and disconnect within seconds.

By coupling Cowrie honeypots with responsive LLM decoders, unknown commands executed by attackers are dynamically rendered with realistic output, prolonging attacker engagement and capturing high-value zero-day payloads for threat intelligence.
